subject: Activation QC: schedule hands-on session + env allowlist & API key checklist
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@edgecraft.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@edgecraft.com, tom.lee@edgecraft.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation QC: schedule hands-on session + env allowlist & API key checklist

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the materials you sent earlier. We're eager to get the hands-on session on the calendar. A few constraints from our side: our security team prefers the POC to run in our staging VPC (private egress) and we need the API keys to be scoped to a sandbox project.

Could you confirm the minimum permissions required for the keys and share the allowlist IP ranges for staging? Also, we'd like a 90-minute session that covers prompt review, routing rules, and one short load test (50 concurrent connections).

Availability this week: Wed 6/16 after 1pm PT or Fri 6/18 morning PT.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Platform, EdgeCraft
--
EdgeCraft Inc.
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@edgecraft.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation QC: schedule hands-on session + env allowlist & API key checklist

Sarah —

Great, thanks. We can run in your staging VPC and will provide scoped sandbox keys. Quick answers below and a suggested plan: 

1) Minimum API key scopes: read:generation, write:kvcache (for request replay), metrics:ingest (for session telemetry). We will provide keys restricted by origin and token caps.

2) Allowlist ranges (staging endpoints): 35.196.0.0/18, 34.96.0.0/14 (these map to our staging frontends in us-west and us-east). If you must restrict to nat IPs we can provide a single egress IP per region — will confirm exact NAT by Wednesday.

3) Load test guidance: we suggest a 12-minute steady ramp to 50 concurrent inference streams, token budgets per stream = 512. We'll monitor latency and fallback triggers.

Suggested session (90 min):
- 0–15m: Introductions + success criteria
- 15–40m: Prompt walkthrough & routing policy demo (canary + fallback)
- 40–70m: Hands-on lab (your staging, keys provided)
- 70–90m: Load test run + results & next steps

Proposed times: Wed 6/16 13:30–15:00 PT or Fri 6/18 09:30–11:00 PT. Which works for your team?

I'll attach our POC tech checklist and a CSV of staging endpoints.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@edgecraft.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00

Thanks Rafael — quick follow-ups from infra: 
- Can the sandbox keys be rotated while the session is running (we test rotation behavior)?
- We need the exact hostnames for the staging endpoints (not only CIDR) to prep our allowlist.

If you can provide hostnames and a short runbook for key rotation I'll get the firewall tickets in today.

Tom

Tom —

Yes, keys can be rotated. We'll issue a short-lived sandbox key for the session (TTL 8 hours) and a follow-up rotated key for validation. Quick hostnames: staging-usw.redwood-infer.net, staging-use.redwood-infer.net.

Attached: EdgeCraft_POC_tech_checklist.pdf (contains rotation runbook, token scopes, sample firewall ticket text). I'll confirm NAT egress IPs by Wed morning.

Can you confirm whether your firewall team needs the hostnames as FQDNs or IPs in the ticket? If FQDNs are acceptable we'll provide those and the CSV attachment for convenience.

Thanks,
Rafael
